mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained unemployment rate increases above 0.3pp for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure, which increases real discount rates and erodes real corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1 million units for four consecutive months signals a housing market downturn, which negatively impacts construction-related sectors and drags on overall equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST remains below 1 million for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A positive year-over-year change in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% combined with a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate by more than 0.2 percentage points signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS YoY change > 0.5% AND UNRATE falls > 0.2pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS grows by more than 0.5% YoY and UNRATE falls by more than 0.2pp simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for two consecutive quarters indicates a broad-based demand shortfall, which depresses earnings expectations across sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when annualized GDPC1 is below 1% for two consecutive quarters.
